steps: Echo-guided pericardiocentesis (or surgical drainage) to relieve tamponade.
IV fluids as a temporising measure to maintain filling.
Avoid positive-pressure ventilation if possible until drained.
Treat and investigate the underlying cause; send pericardial fluid for analysis.

drugRefs.dose: 250–500 mL bolus, repeated to clinical response
drugRefs.why: Temporising measure only — augments preload/right-heart filling to maintain cardiac output until definitive pericardiocentesis. Definitive treatment is drainage, not drugs.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Pericardial Disease and Cardiac Tamponade
2015 ESC Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Pericardial Diseases

confirm: Hypotension, raised JVP, muffled heart sounds (Beck's triad) with pulsus paradoxus; echo shows effusion with diastolic collapse.
